breakthroughs.title: Lean-Verified Disproof of the Caiolo–Ferroni–Hoster Dual Chow Conjecture for Matroids

Proved the exact sharp rank threshold: dual Chow real-rootedness holds for all matroids of rank r if and only if r ≤ 4.
Fully formalized in Lean 4.35.0 with Mathlib matroids plus an independent exact SymPy certificate, published openly on GitHub and X.
breakthroughs.caveats: Unrefereed open-internet release (X + GitHub); internally audited with Lean 4 and SymPy replay scripts, while independent matroid-theorist journal review and priority checks remain open.

breakthroughs.summary: Bogdan Georgiev, Javier Gómez-Serrano, Terence Tao, and Adam Zsolt Wagner benchmarked Google DeepMind’s AlphaEvolve on 67 open mathematical optimization and construction problems. technicalHighlights: Systematically evaluated autonomous evolutionary code search across 67 open problems spanning analysis, combinatorics, geometry, and number theory.
Improved multiple long-standing human bounds and synthesized general closed-form constructions validated by AlphaProof and Deep Think.
Published in PNAS (2026), establishing a scalable methodology for mathematician-AI collaboration.
breakthroughs.caveats: Strongest on extremal and constructive problems with fast programmatic scoring functions; conceptual structural proofs still required coupling with separate proof systems.

scoreRationale.ripple: Provided the operational blueprint for coupling evolutionary search with formal provers across academia.

breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Physics-informed neural networks discovered new families of unstable self-similar blow-up singularities in 3D Euler and porous-media fluid PDEs at GPU double-precision accuracy.
breakthroughs.summary: Researchers from NYU, Google DeepMind, Stanford, and Brown paired physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) with a high-precision Gauss–Newton optimizer to locate elusive unstable self-similar blow-up profiles in nonlinear fluid equations. Reaching near-double-float machine precision (~10⁻¹³ residual), the discovered profiles cross the precision threshold required for rigorous computer-assisted mathematical blow-up proofs and revealed a clean asymptotic scaling law.
technicalHighlights: Discovered multiple new families of unstable self-similar blow-up solutions for 3D Euler with boundary and incompressible porous media (IPM) equations.
Achieved near-double-float GPU round-off accuracy, overcoming the ~10⁻³ error ceiling that previously barred PINNs from rigorous PDE proofs.
Uncovered an empirical asymptotic law relating blow-up rate to instability order, informing subsequent Navier–Stokes blow-up research.
breakthroughs.caveats: Supplies ultra-high-precision numerical profiles rather than complete formal proofs on its own; rigorous existence proofs require follow-up interval-arithmetic certification.

scoreRationale.ripple: Provided a key computational playbook directly feeding 2026 computer-assisted attacks on Euler and Navier–Stokes blow-up.

breakthroughs.title: Evo 2: 40B Genomic Foundation Model & Viable AI-Designed Genomes
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Trained on 9.3 trillion nucleotides across all domains of life with a 1M base-pair context, enabling zero-shot pathogenic variant prediction and wet-lab-viable AI-designed viral genomes.
breakthroughs.summary: Arc Institute, Stanford, and NVIDIA released Evo 2, a 40-billion-parameter open-source genomic foundation model trained on 9.3 trillion base pairs from over 100,000 species across prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Handling 1-million-nucleotide contexts via the StripedHyena 2 architecture, Evo 2 predicts human BRCA1 pathogenicity without task-specific training, exposes interpretable biological features (α-helices, β-sheets, exon boundaries), and by 2026 guided the chemical synthesis of viable AI-designed bacteriophage genomes capable of lysing E. coli.
technicalHighlights: 1-million-base-pair context window spans entire microbial genomes and long-range eukaryotic regulatory loci.
Mechanistic interpretability (with Goodfire) revealed learned internal representations of 3D protein secondary structure straight from raw DNA.
Downstream 2026 wet-lab validation synthesized 285 Evo-designed ΦX174 phage genomes, with 16 actively inhibiting E. coli.
breakthroughs.caveats: Viability drops steeply as generated sequences diverge from natural evolutionary neighborhoods; eukaryotic whole-genome design raises biosecurity governance challenges (prompting exclusion of human-pathogenic viruses from training).

Discovered explicit, externally verifiable Lyapunov functions for 12.7% of random non-polynomial dynamical systems.
Validated backward synthetic data generation as a general template for neural mathematical discovery.

breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First AI-discovered fundamental computer science routines merged into the standard LLVM C++ sorting library, running trillions of times daily worldwide.
breakthroughs.summary: By framing assembly-instruction synthesis as a single-player game rewarding both exact correctness and low CPU latency, DeepMind’s AlphaDev discovered instruction-saving tricks ("AlphaDev swap and copy moves") overlooked by human compiler engineers for decades. Its sort-3/4/5 routines accelerated short sequences up to 70% and were merged into LLVM libc++, alongside a 30%-faster hashing routine adopted in Google’s Abseil library.
technicalHighlights: Discovered branchless assembly instruction sequences reducing sort-3 and sort-5 instruction counts below decades-old human baselines.
Merged into LLVM libc++ standard library and Google Abseil, achieving real-world production deployment across billions of devices.
Verified exact equivalence across all permutation inputs and microarchitectural latency benchmarks.
breakthroughs.caveats: Improvements target fixed-length base-case sorting networks (3–5 elements) and short hashing keys rather than asymptotically faster general sorting algorithms.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved RL can invent non-obvious instruction-level algorithmic primitives from scratch.
scoreRationale.ripple: Deployed directly into LLVM libc++ and Abseil, executing trillions of times daily across global computing infrastructure.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature and exhaustively verified for functional equivalence in production compilers.
scoreRationale.velocity: Surpassed decades of manual micro-optimization in standard library sorting primitives.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaTensor: Reinforcement Learning Discovers Faster Matrix Multiplication
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First AI system to surpass a 50-year human algorithmic record in core mathematics—finding a 47-multiplication 4×4 algorithm in mod 2 and 14,000+ novel factorizations.
breakthroughs.summary: Published in Nature (Vol. 610), DeepMind's AlphaTensor framed matrix multiplication as a single-player 3D tensor-decomposition game played by an AlphaZero-style reinforcement learning agent. It improved the best-known scalar multiplication count for over 70 matrix sizes—including beating Volker Strassen's iconic 1969 49-multiplication 4×4 algorithm with 47 multiplications in finite-field arithmetic (ℤ₂)—while also optimizing hardware-specific GPU/TPU kernels.
technicalHighlights: Reduced 4×4 matrix multiplication in mod-2 arithmetic from Strassen's 49 multiplications (1969) to 47.
Discovered >14,000 non-equivalent rank-49 4×4 factorizations, revealing unexpected richness in algebraic complexity.
Pioneered the autonomous algorithm-discovery lineage culminating in FunSearch (2023) and AlphaEvolve (2025).
breakthroughs.caveats: The 47-multiplication 4×4 breakthrough held in finite-field (characteristic 2) arithmetic rather than real/complex numbers—a gap later closed by AlphaEvolve's 48-multiplication complex algorithm in 2025.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved deep RL can autonomously discover mathematically novel, provably exact fundamental algorithms beyond human intuition.
scoreRationale.ripple: Launched the AI-for-algorithm-discovery subfield directly leading to AlphaDev, FunSearch, and AlphaEvolve.
scoreRationale.verification: Every tensor factorization is algebraically exact, published in Nature, and openly released for deterministic checking.
scoreRationale.velocity: Broke a 53-year algorithmic standstill and accelerated automated search across discrete math.

breakthroughs.title: Autonomous Deep Reinforcement Learning Control of Tokamak Fusion Plasmas
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First autonomous deep reinforcement learning system to command real-time magnetic coils inside a live nuclear fusion tokamak, sculpting novel plasma geometries.
breakthroughs.summary: DeepMind and EPFL’s Swiss Plasma Center trained a deep reinforcement learning controller in simulation and deployed it zero-shot onto the TCV tokamak in Lausanne. Controlling 19 magnetic coils at 10 kHz, the AI autonomously shaped and stabilized complex fusion plasmas—including elongated, negative-triangularity, snowflake, and simultaneous dual-plasma "droplet" configurations.
technicalHighlights: Replaced hand-engineered decoupled PID controller stacks with a single end-to-end neural policy acting at 100-microsecond intervals.
Stabilized exotic advanced divertor geometries (snowflake and dual-droplet plasmas) in physical tokamak shots.
Proved sim-to-real transfer of autonomous AI control onto one of experimental physics’ most unforgiving nonlinear systems.
breakthroughs.caveats: Demonstrated on the research-scale TCV tokamak rather than a net-energy burning plasma reactor; scaling to ITER-class thermal loads requires additional safety guarantees.

scoreRationale.foundational: Pioneered end-to-end learned physical control for high-temperature magnetized fusion plasmas.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly influenced subsequent AI-controlled fusion experiments across tokamaks worldwide (including WEST and DIII-D).
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature with live experimental validation on TCV reactor hardware.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed months of bespoke control-engineering design per plasma shape into rapid automated policy synthesis.

breakthroughs.title: AI-Guided Discovery of New Theorems in Knot Theory & Representation Theory
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: First landmark Nature demonstration that machine learning attribution can guide pure mathematicians to discover and prove wholly new theorems across topology and algebra.
breakthroughs.summary: Google DeepMind partnered with mathematicians at Oxford and Sydney to train neural networks on mathematical invariants and apply saliency attribution to surface hidden relationships. The framework led directly to a new theorem linking the algebraic signature and geometric natural slope of hyperbolic knots, plus a new candidate algorithm for Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials advancing the 40-year-old combinatorial invariance conjecture.
technicalHighlights: Discovered and rigorously proved a new quantitative connection between hyperbolic knot geometry (natural slope) and algebraic knot signature.
Identified a salient subgraph structure predicting Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials from Bruhat intervals, advancing Lusztig and Dyer’s combinatorial invariance conjecture.
Established the "human intuition guided by ML attribution" workflow that preceded generative LLM theorem discovery.
breakthroughs.caveats: Neural networks surfaced patterns and candidate conjectures rather than writing formal proofs; human mathematicians formulated and proved the final theorems.

scoreRationale.foundational: Established genuine peer-reviewed theorems in pure math via ML-guided conjecture generation.
scoreRationale.ripple: Catalyzed the modern AI-for-pure-mathematics movement and human-AI conjecture loops.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Nature with complete human-verified mathematical proofs.
scoreRationale.velocity: Opened a new discovery paradigm years before reasoning LLMs could write formal proofs.

breakthroughs.title: AlphaFold 2: Atomic-Accuracy Protein Structure Prediction (CASP14)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Solved biology's 50-year protein structure prediction grand challenge at atomic accuracy—earning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry and establishing the modern AI-for-science benchmark.
breakthroughs.summary: Validated at the blind CASP14 competition in November 2020 and published in Nature (July 2021), DeepMind's AlphaFold 2 introduced the Evoformer and equivariant structure modules to predict 3D atomic coordinates of proteins directly from amino-acid sequences with accuracy rivaling X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM. Releasing open source code and >200 million predicted structures in the AlphaFold Protein Structure Database permanently transformed structural biology and served as the blueprint for the entire 2020s wave of scientific AI.
technicalHighlights: Achieved ~0.96 Å median backbone RMSD on blind CASP14 targets, effectively solving single-chain static protein folding.
Awarded half of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry (Demis Hassabis and John Jumper).
Open-source release and EMBL-EBI database unlocked >200 million structures used by millions of researchers worldwide.
breakthroughs.caveats: Predicts static single-chain conformations rather than dynamic conformational ensembles, multi-ligand complexes, or folding pathways—gaps subsequently targeted by AlphaFold 3 and generative biology models.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved a 50-year grand challenge in molecular biology and proved deep learning can crack core scientific physics problems.
scoreRationale.ripple: One of the highest-impact scientific tools of the 21st century—directly catalyzing AlphaFold 3, AlphaProteo, Evo 2, and modern drug discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Blind CASP14 benchmark victory, landmark Nature paper, tens of thousands of independent experimental confirmations, and the 2024 Nobel Prize.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed months-to-years of crystallography per protein into minutes of computation.

breakthroughs.title: Halicin: First Broad-Spectrum Antibiotic Discovered via Deep Learning
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Nine months before AlphaFold 2, a deep graph neural network screened >107 million molecules and discovered a structurally novel antibiotic effective against pan-resistant pathogens.
breakthroughs.summary: MIT and Broad Institute researchers trained a directed message-passing graph neural network (Chemprop) on bacterial growth-inhibition assays and screened the Drug Repurposing Hub and over 107 million compounds from ZINC15. The model surfaced halicin—a molecule structurally divergent from conventional antibiotics that disrupts bacterial membrane proton motive force and cleared multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii and C. difficile infections in mouse models.
technicalHighlights: Trained Chemprop message-passing GNN on 2,335 molecules, then virtually screened >107 million structures in days.
Identified halicin, structurally distinct from all known antibiotic classes, showing potent activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis and carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae.
Demonstrated zero detectable resistance emergence in E. coli over a 30-day serial passage assay and launched the MIT Antibiotics-AI Project.
breakthroughs.caveats: Halicin itself faced systemic toxicity hurdles during follow-up preclinical translation, motivating subsequent narrow-spectrum AI antibiotics such as abaucin (2023) and explainable structural-class screens.
institutions: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

scoreRationale.foundational: Established deep graph neural networks as a practical wet-lab drug discovery engine capable of finding structurally novel antimicrobial mechanisms.
scoreRationale.ripple: Catalyzed an entire wave of AI-guided antimicrobial and small-molecule discovery pipelines across academia and pharma.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Cell with extensive in vitro assays, resistance-evolution testing, and in vivo mouse infection clearance models.
scoreRationale.velocity: Virtually screened >107 million candidate molecules in days, compressing early-stage antimicrobial hit identification by orders of magnitude.

breakthroughs.title: Boolean Pythagorean Triples Problem Solved via Cube-and-Conquer SAT
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Pioneering pre-neural symbolic AI milestone: resolved a 30-year Ramsey theory problem via a 200-terabyte machine-verified SAT proof.
breakthroughs.summary: Marijn Heule, Oliver Kullmann, and Victor Marek encoded Ronald Graham’s longstanding Boolean Pythagorean Triples problem—whether the positive integers can be 2-colored with no monochromatic solution to a² + b² = c²—into propositional logic and solved it via Cube-and-Conquer SAT search. The solver proved 1..7,824 is 2-colorable while 1..7,825 is impossible, producing a 200 TB DRAT proof certificate later formally verified in Coq.
technicalHighlights: Partitioned the search space into one million sub-problems (“cubes”) solved in two days across 800 cores on the Stampede supercomputer.
Established the exact threshold at n = 7,825—the largest mathematical proof certificate generated up to that time (200 TB uncompressed, 68 GB compressed).
Independently verified by formal checkers extracted from Coq, proving symbolic search could settle open combinatorial problems beyond human casework.
breakthroughs.caveats: A pure classical SAT/symbolic search milestone rather than deep learning; while 100% machine-verified, the 200 TB proof offers little human-readable structural intuition and required bespoke symmetry breaking.

scoreRationale.foundational: Settled a famous open Ramsey theory conjecture posed by Ronald Graham and established the exact critical coloring threshold.
scoreRationale.ripple: Demonstrated scalable machine-checked proof certificates (DRAT) and directly foreshadowed hybrid formal-verification pipelines.
scoreRationale.verification: Machine-checked via DRAT certificates and independently verified in Coq—gold-standard formal certainty.
scoreRationale.velocity: Solved a 30-year open problem in two days of parallel symbolic search, yet remained restricted to finite combinatorial encodings.

breakthroughs.title: Robot Scientist “Adam” Autonomously Discovers New Yeast Gene Functions
breakthroughs.aiSystem: Robot Scientist Adam (Abductive Logic + Lab Robotics)
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: Historic pre-neural benchmark: the first closed-loop autonomous AI system to formulate hypotheses, run physical lab experiments, and publish new biological knowledge.
breakthroughs.summary: Developed by Ross King and colleagues at Aberystwyth and Cambridge, Robot Scientist “Adam” combined symbolic abductive logic programming, formal biological ontologies, and automated wet-lab robotics to investigate orphan enzymes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Without human intervention in the loop, Adam formulated 20 hypotheses identifying genes encoding orphan enzymes, designed and executed growth assays, confirmed 12 hypotheses, and had its key discoveries independently validated by manual human biochemistry.
technicalHighlights: First physical machine to execute the full scientific method autonomously—hypothesis generation, experiment design, wet-lab execution, and result interpretation.
Identified three previously unannotated yeast genes encoding the orphan enzyme 2-aminoadipate transaminase (confirmed manually via wet-lab enzyme assays).
Demonstrated end-to-end formalization of experimental metadata and reasoning decades before LLM-based AI Co-Scientists.
breakthroughs.caveats: Relied on rigid symbolic logic rules and domain-specific yeast ontologies; it could not generalize outside narrowly encoded metabolic models—highlighting why modern neural foundation models triggered a phase transition.

scoreRationale.foundational: Proved in principle that an autonomous AI system can independently discover genuine new empirical scientific knowledge.
scoreRationale.ripple: Inspired the entire self-driving laboratory and autonomous AI scientist movement, culminating in systems like Google AI Co-Scientist.
scoreRationale.verification: Published in Science with human wet-lab biochemical verification of Adam’s newly discovered gene–enzyme mappings.
scoreRationale.velocity: Pioneered automated experimental cycles, though narrow symbolic engineering kept throughput modest compared to 2025–2026 foundation models.

breakthroughs.title: Automated Theorem Prover EQP Solves the 63-Year-Old Robbins Conjecture
breakthroughs.whyItMatters: The foundational pre-neural milestone in autonomous AI mathematics: solved a 63-year-old algebra conjecture that defeated Alfred Tarski.
breakthroughs.summary: Posed by Herbert Robbins in 1933 and studied unsuccessfully by Alfred Tarski and generations of algebraists, the Robbins Conjecture asked whether every Robbins algebra is a Boolean algebra. On October 10, 1996, William McCune’s specialized symbolic equational prover EQP at Argonne National Laboratory autonomously discovered a complete proof in eight days on a workstation, outputting a machine-checked proof object later simplified and formalized in Isabelle/HOL.
technicalHighlights: Used associative-commutative (AC) unification and paramodulation strategies in EQP to prove Winker’s sufficient condition automatically.
First widely celebrated resolution of a longstanding open mathematical conjecture by a fully autonomous computer reasoning program.
Produced a complete machine-verifiable proof object checked independently, later streamlined by Dahn (1998) and formalized in the Archive of Formal Proofs.
breakthroughs.caveats: Required extensive human algebraic reductions (Winker’s lemmas) and hand-crafted equational search heuristics; pure symbolic provers remained largely isolated to narrow algebraic/logic niches for the next two decades until neural networks arrived.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved a famous 63-year-old foundational algebra problem that resisted Alfred Tarski and decades of human mathematicians.
scoreRationale.ripple: Became the canonical proof-of-concept for automated mathematical discovery, directly motivating generations of ATP and formal verification research.
scoreRationale.verification: Produced a machine-checked formal proof object verified by independent checkers and published in the Journal of Automated Reasoning.
scoreRationale.velocity: Closed a 63-year open problem in 8 days of workstation search—though symbolic provers only achieved a handful of such wins across the next 24 years.
